title: Confirm button is red to deactivate and blue to activate
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BTNCOL-01) is tracked at {Location-A} and is active.
  • Inventory part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BTNCOL-02) is tracked at {Location-A} and is inactive.
  • {Part-A} and {Part-B} share the start of their numbers (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BTNCOL-0), so one search lists them together.
custom_steps:
1. Open {Part-A}, pick "Inactive", click Save and look at the confirmation's buttons; click "Cancel" and close the dialog.
  2. On the Inactive tab open {Part-B}, pick "Active", click Save and look at the buttons; click "Cancel" and close the dialog.
  3. On the Active tab turn on "Deactivate parts", tick {Part-A}, click "Deactivate" and look at the buttons; click "Cancel" and × on the bar.
  4. On the Inactive tab turn on "Activate parts", tick {Part-B}, click "Activate" and look at the buttons; click "Cancel".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: A red "Deactivate" button, with "Cancel" to its left.
  • Step 2: A blue "Activate" button, with "Cancel" to its left.
  • Step 3: A red "Deactivate" button, with "Cancel" to its left.
  • Step 4: A blue "Activate" button, with "Cancel" to its left. No part changed status.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S10-R11, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas boards 3.3, 3.7, 4.4 and 4.7, 13 Oct copy. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S10-R11: “The confirm button reads "Deactivate" in red for a deactivation and "Activate" in blue for a reactivation. Cancel sits to its left.”
